notes: Dev ABox contraction paired with technology-replace-d001 (Windows Vista's predecessor, Windows XP -> Windows 95): it removes the revision's original fact, 'Windows Vista is the direct successor of Windows XP.', on successor_of, which is tagged functional (within one product line a version directly succeeds one version), so the cardinality question is a functional 'no' that becomes 'I don't know'. Known limit of the functional reading: Windows XP is given as the direct successor of both Windows 2000 and Windows Me (the NT and 9x lines merged in XP; Wikipedia: 'It is a direct successor to Windows 2000 for high-end and business users and Windows Me for home users'), so the relation check is worded 'within a single product line'; Vista has one predecessor. The candidate is Windows Server 2003 (a release dated between XP and Vista, with no stored successor claim that rules Vista out): Windows 98 was dropped because its own successor Windows Me and its date (nine years before Vista) let a model hold 'no' without Vista's predecessor; Windows 95 and Windows 2000 sit next to XP in text; Windows 7 follows Vista by dating alone. Related near is the inverse (XP as Vista's direct predecessor, yes then I don't know); related far binds Vista through its code name Longhorn, as in the revision. The two 2-hop derived questions go through the removed fact by description ('the direct predecessor of Windows Vista') and look up a fact stored about Windows XP by name (its code name Whistler, its release year 2001). The NT-kernel question of the revision was dropped: Vista is itself Windows NT 6.0 and follows the NT 5.x releases, so 'yes' has a route back that does not use the removed fact; the Start-menu question was dropped because its 'no' about XP is stored independently. Evidence: the infini-gram API (v4_dolma-v1_7_llama) answered on 2026-11-12, so the new counts are real; the older counts are the ones of the paired revision record (same fact, same evidence). The cardinality question has no corpus count (the functional tag's relation check carries it); 'Vista's predecessor, Windows Server 2003' occurs 0 times. Unrelated near shares the subject; delete is exempt from Rule 7.
